correctness.rationale: Assume strictly positive orbit tending to (0,0), f C1 near zero and q=f(0) strictly between 0 and 1. Eventual x contraction x_{n+1}<=rho x_n and y_{n+1}<=rho x_n yields exponential decay. Thus sum (j+1)|delta_j|<infinity, sum |phi_j|<infinity, giving exact positive finite C and D by weighted logarithmic telescoping. Exact identity y_{n+1}=x_{n+1}(e^{a y_n}-1) leads to log y_n=log D+n log(aC)+n(n+1)log(q)/2+o(1). For Ricker f(x)=exp(r(1-x)(x-b)), 0<x0<b is invariant, strictly contracting; log rates and first eta-hitting clocks follow with O(1) integer effects. Independent numerical logarithmic iteration checked finite constants; proof rests on summable errors, not finite runs.
